LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 DETERMINERS: NUMERALS AND ORDINALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.3: Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Determiners: Numerals and Ordinals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Determiners: Numerals and Ordinals, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we identify numerals and ordinals? 2. Why do we use numerals and ordinals in sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Determiners: Numerals and Ordinals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: confidence in correct use numerals and ordinals as determiners in communication.

● Communication: writing skill is developed when constructing sentences using numerals and ordinals as determiners with

peers.

Values:
Unity: the learner harmoniously works with peers to construct sentences with numerals and ordinals as determiners.

Link to other subjects

The learner relates the concept of Numerals and ordinals to number work in mathematics.
